meta.document_purpose: Self-contained specification. Feeding this JSON back to a design/dev agent (human or AI) must be enough to rebuild the exact visual system without re-explaining anything.

source_mockups.flecto: Rental-business SaaS landing. Deep forest green + mint accents, cream/off-white sections, rounded blob shapes, soft organic illustration, friendly fintech tone, rounded pill CTAs.
source_mockups.orderful: EDI trading-platform landing. White canvas, black type, one vivid red-orange accent, thin-line node/dotted network diagrams, sharp edges, dense data grids, monospace-flavored numerals, technical/engineering tone.

assumptions_not_specified_by_user: Exact product name/domain of the target web app was not given; tokens below are product-agnostic and ready to receive real copy.

Exact hex values were not dictated by the user beyond 'max 2 predominant colors + black/white tints of them' — the two hues below are derived from the fused mockups (Flecto green + Orderful red-orange) and are tunable without breaking the system.
Underline (<u>) is included per the user's explicit accessibility/native-HTML request, but is restricted to non-link emphasis to avoid conflicting with the browser-native meaning of underline = link.

concept.definition: Raw, high-contrast, grid-exposed, monospace-inflected interface language (from Orderful) softened by exactly one inherited gesture from Flecto: fully-rounded pill shapes reserved ONLY for interactive/status elements (buttons, tags, badges, dots). Everything structural stays sharp (0 radius).

inherit_from_orderful: visible hairline borders/grid lines as decoration
inherit_from_flecto: fully-rounded pill shape reserved for buttons/badges/tags/status-dots only
warm off-white ('paper') as the light-mode base instead of pure white
friendly, generous section padding despite the brutalist grid
discard: Orderful's dense multi-column text-heavy sections (not compatible with no-scroll constraint)

page_behavior.scroll: none — the welcome page is a single viewport screen (100dvh), not a scrolling composition
page_behavior.viewport_strategy: All typography and spacing are fluid (clamp()) so the hero content always fits 100dvh at every breakpoint instead of being scaled by fixed breakpoints
page_behavior.animation_character: Subtle, functional, on-load only (staggered fade/translate + drawing dotted connector lines) plus micro-interactions on hover/focus. No scroll-triggered or parallax effects — there is no scroll to trigger from.
page_behavior.signature_motif: A node-link diagram (dotted/dashed lines connecting small square or circular nodes, labeled with JetBrains Mono micro-text) as the hero's visual centerpiece — fusion of Flecto's flow-connector boxes and Orderful's dotted network diagram.

color.rule: Exactly 2 predominant hues. Every other color (backgrounds, borders, disabled states, 'black', 'white') is a tint or shade generated from these same 2 hues — never a neutral gray.

primary.name: Signal Green
primary.role: Brand identity, primary CTA, success/positive state, links

secondary.name: Signal Red-Orange
secondary.role: Accent, urgency/highlight, secondary CTA, data emphasis, focus/alert state

derived_neutrals.rule: 'White' and 'black' are NOT pure grayscale — they are heavily desaturated tints of the two brand hues, alternating by mode.

paper.description: Near-white neutral, warm tint of secondary hue (nods to Flecto's cream + Orderful's white)

ink.description: Near-black neutral, cool tint of primary hue (technobrutalist dark canvas)

color.usage_rule: Never use both primary and secondary at full saturation in the same component at the same visual weight — one always leads, the other is a single accent touch (a dot, an underline, one CTA).

font_primary.usage: UI chrome, headings, nav, buttons, labels, eyebrow tags
font_primary.source: self-hosted variable font recommended (woff2), font-display: swap

font_secondary.usage: Body paragraphs, stat numerals, data readouts, code-like microcopy, eyebrow badges, form inputs — deliberate technical voice
font_secondary.fallback_stack: 'JetBrains Mono', 'JetBrains Mono Fallback', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace

scale.method: Geometric progression using the golden ratio (phi = 1.618, phi^-1 = 0.618)
scale.fluid_note: --text-4xl (hero headline) MUST use clamp() since the page has no scroll — it must never overflow 100dvh on short viewports.

native_emphasis_rules.bold: Use <strong> for genuine importance, never <b> or font-weight alone — screen readers announce <strong>.
native_emphasis_rules.italic: Use <em> for stressed emphasis, never <i> alone.
native_emphasis_rules.underline: Reserve real <a> underlines for links only. For non-link emphasis, wrap in <u> AND add a visual differentiator (color or dotted style) so it is never mistaken for a link — this is the one place 'native HTML underline' and accessibility best-practice must be reconciled explicitly.

asymmetric_grid_split.description: Hero uses a 61.8% / 38.2% two-column split — wide column for the node-link diagram/visual, narrow column for headline + CTA, mirroring both mockups' off-center compositions
asymmetric_grid_split.css: grid-template-columns: 0.618fr 1fr;  /* or 38.2% 61.8% depending on which side leads at each breakpoint */

spacing_scale.method: Same phi ladder as typography, base 0.5rem

breakpoints_mobile_first.note: Author base styles for mobile with no media query; add min-width queries upward only, never max-width

no_scroll_technique.sizing: every font-size, gap and section padding in the hero MUST be clamp()-based, not fixed, so the layout compresses gracefully on short/landscape mobile viewports instead of overflowing
no_scroll_technique.verification: test at 100dvh on: 360x640 (small mobile), 768x1024 (tablet portrait), 1440x900 (laptop), 1920x1080 (desktop) — nothing may require scrolling at any of these

iconography.usage_rule: Icons inherit currentColor; never hardcode icon fill/stroke color. Prefer inlined SVG (lucide's raw source) over an icon-font or extra HTTP requests.

motion.philosophy: Subtle and functional, never decorative for its own sake — every animation communicates state or draws attention exactly once

easing.note: avoid bouncy/elastic curves — technobrutalism moves with precision, not playfulness

motion.entrance_pattern: On load: staggered fade + 8px translate-Y for headline/CTA (stagger 60ms per item), then the node-link diagram's dashed lines draw in via stroke-dashoffset over 600–900ms
motion.micro_interactions: Buttons: 120ms background/border shift. Links/underline emphasis: 120ms underline-offset shift. Focus: instant ring, no transition delay.
motion.reduced_motion: Wrap all non-essential motion in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference); reduced-motion users get instant state changes only

corner_radius_rule.structural_elements: 0px — cards, sections, containers, inputs stay sharp
corner_radius_rule.interactive_pill_elements: 9999px — reserved exclusively for buttons, tags, badges, status dots (the one inherited Flecto gesture)

visual_motifs.borders: 1px solid var(--color-border) as a visible structural/decorative element, not just a container edge — used to expose the grid intentionally
visual_motifs.hero_diagram: dotted/dashed connector lines (stroke-dasharray) linking small square or circular nodes; nodes labeled in --font-secondary micro-text
visual_motifs.eyebrow_badge: uppercase, --font-secondary, --text-xs, 0.12em letter-spacing, inside a 9999px-radius pill outlined 1px
visual_motifs.stat_block: oversized numeral in --font-secondary + --text-3xl/4xl paired with a small uppercase --font-primary label beneath it

accessibility.contrast_targets: WCAG AA minimum (4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text/UI); verify every primary/secondary ramp step actually used for text against its background
accessibility.semantic_html: header/nav/main/section/footer as real landmarks; <button> for actions, <a> only for navigation; <dialog> for modals; <details>/<summary> for any disclosure widget instead of custom JS accordions
accessibility.focus_visible: always a visible focus ring using --color-focus-ring, never suppressed with outline:none without a replacement
accessibility.language_attribute: html lang attribute must be updated whenever the i18n language toggle changes

structure_and_components.philosophy: Functional and simple — prefer a native HTML element over a custom-built one whenever one exists
preferred_native_elements: form + native validation attributes (required, pattern, type=email)
welcome_page_sections_no_scroll: hero (eyebrow + headline + subcopy + primary CTA + node-link diagram)
optional: single row of 2-3 stat_blocks if space allows within 100dvh

code_philosophy.naming_and_comments_language: English, standardized, regardless of the product's display language
code_philosophy.css_approach: Vanilla CSS only, no preprocessor required. Always author via CSS custom properties (var(--token)) — no hardcoded hex/px values in component rules.
code_philosophy.custom_properties_scope: :root for global tokens, [data-theme] attribute overrides for theme variants
code_philosophy.cleanliness_rule: No unused abstractions, no premature component variants — build only what the single welcome-page surface currently needs

internationalization.html_wiring: data-i18n="hero.headline" attributes on elements, resolved by a small vanilla loader that fetches the active language JSON and sets textContent — no framework required
internationalization.language_switch_persistence: selected language is part of the storable appearance config below

appearance_settings.apply_mechanism: On load, read localStorage config, set data-theme and lang attributes on <html> before first paint (inline blocking script) to avoid flash of wrong theme/language

performance_optimization.fonts: self-host Inter + JetBrains Mono woff2, preload the exact weights used, font-display: swap
performance_optimization.css: single vanilla stylesheet, critical-path CSS is the whole file since the entire page is above-the-fold (no-scroll) by definition
performance_optimization.icons: inline lucide SVGs directly, no icon-font, no per-icon HTTP request
performance_optimization.animation: prefer CSS transitions/animations over JS-driven motion; only the dashed-line draw-in may need a small JS trigger (IntersectionObserver is unnecessary since there's no scroll — trigger on DOMContentLoaded instead)
performance_optimization.images: hero is vector/SVG based (node-link diagram) — avoids raster image weight entirely on the one screen that must load instantly
